subject: math
cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable

items.prompt: Find the median of the data set $\{3, 5, 8, 11, 14\}$.

steps: The data are already sorted: $3, 5, 8, 11, 14$.
There are $n=5$ values, an odd count, so the median is the single middle value.
The middle (3rd) value is $8$.
The median is $8$.

items.prompt: Find the mean of the data set $\{2, 4, 6, 8, 10\}$.

steps: Add the values: $2+4+6+8+10=30$.
Divide by the number of values $n=5$: $\bar{x}=\frac{30}{5}$.
The mean is $6$.

items.prompt: Find the range of the data set $\{7, 12, 15, 20, 23\}$.

steps: The range is the maximum value minus the minimum value.
Maximum $=23$ and minimum $=7$.
The range is $16$.

items.prompt: A dot plot of the number of pets owned by students piles up at the low values ($0$ and $1$) and stretches out with a long tail toward the high values ($6$, $7$, $8$). Describe the shape of this distribution.

steps: The bulk of the data sits at the low end (most students own $0$ or $1$ pet).
The tail, the part that stretches out, points toward the high values.
A distribution is named for the side its tail points to, not where the bulk sits.
Because the tail points to the right (high) side, the distribution is skewed right.

items.prompt: Find the median of the data set $\{10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30\}$.

steps: The data are sorted: $10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30$.
There are $n=6$ values, an even count, so the median is the average of the two middle values.
The two middle (3rd and 4th) values are $18$ and $22$.

items.prompt: For the data set $\{4, 6, 9, 10, 13, 15, 18, 21\}$, find $Q_1$, $Q_3$, and the $\text{IQR}$.

steps: The data are sorted with $n=8$ values. The median splits them into a lower half $\{4,6,9,10\}$ and an upper half $\{13,15,18,21\}$.
$Q_1$ is the median of the lower half: $\frac{6+9}{2}=\frac{15}{2}=7.5$.
$Q_3$ is the median of the upper half: $\frac{15+18}{2}=\frac{33}{2}=16.5$.

items.prompt: A data set has $Q_1=14$ and $Q_3=26$, so $\text{IQR}=12$. Using the $1.5\times\text{IQR}$ rule, is the value $46$ an outlier?
items.answer: Yes, $46$ is an outlier (it exceeds the upper fence of $44$).

steps: The upper fence is $Q_3+1.5\cdot\text{IQR}$.
Compute $1.5\cdot\text{IQR}=1.5\cdot 12=18$.
Upper fence $=26+18=44$.
Since $46>44$, the value lies beyond the fence, so $46$ is an outlier.

items.prompt: The values $\{6, 7, 8, 9, 10\}$ have mean $8$. The value $10$ is replaced with $30$. What is the new mean?

steps: Replacing $10$ with $30$ gives the data set $\{6, 7, 8, 9, 30\}$.
Add the new values: $6+7+8+9+30=60$.
Divide by $n=5$: $\bar{x}=\frac{60}{5}=12$.
The new mean is $12$ (the outlier pulled the mean up from $8$).

items.prompt: For a data set, the mean is $\bar{x}=72$ and the median is $58$. Based on the relationship between the mean and the median, describe the likely shape of the distribution.

steps: Compare the mean and the median: here the mean ($72$) is greater than the median ($58$).
The mean is pulled in the direction of the longer tail, while the median resists it.
When the mean exceeds the median, the tail stretches toward the high values.
A tail toward the high (right) side means the distribution is skewed right.

items.prompt: For the data set $\{12, 15, 15, 18, 20, 22, 24, 27, 30, 31\}$, find the median and the $\text{IQR}$.

steps: The data are sorted with $n=10$ values. The median is the average of the 5th and 6th values: $\frac{20+22}{2}=\frac{42}{2}=21$.
The lower half is $\{12,15,15,18,20\}$; its median is the middle value, $Q_1=15$.
The upper half is $\{22,24,27,30,31\}$; its median is the middle value, $Q_3=27$.

items.prompt: Home prices in a neighborhood are strongly skewed right because a few mansions sell for far more than the typical home. Which measure of center and which measure of spread best summarize these prices, and why?
items.answer: The median and the $\text{IQR}$, because they are resistant to the extreme high values and skew.

steps: The data are strongly skewed right with a few very large values (the mansions), which act as outliers.
The mean and the range are both pulled upward by extreme values, so they would overstate a typical price and the typical spread.
The median and the $\text{IQR}$ are resistant: they depend on the position of the data, not the size of extreme values.
Therefore the median best summarizes the center and the $\text{IQR}$ best summarizes the spread.

items.prompt: Class A's test scores have median $78$ and $\text{IQR}=6$. Class B's scores have median $78$ and $\text{IQR}=20$. Compare the two distributions and state which class had more consistent scores.
items.answer: Both classes have the same center, but Class A is more consistent because its $\text{IQR}$ ($6$) is much smaller than Class B's ($20$).

steps: Both classes share the same median, $78$, so their centers are equal.
The $\text{IQR}$ measures spread: a smaller $\text{IQR}$ means the middle $50\%$ of scores are packed more tightly together.
Class A has $\text{IQR}=6$, far smaller than Class B's $\text{IQR}=20$, so Class A's scores vary less.
Equal centers do not mean equal distributions: Class A is more consistent, while Class B's scores are much more spread out.

items.prompt: A data set has $Q_1=20$ and $Q_3=32$. What is the smallest value that would be flagged as a high outlier by the $1.5\times\text{IQR}$ rule? (Give the upper fence; values strictly greater than it are outliers.)
items.answer: The upper fence is $50$ (values greater than $50$ are outliers).

steps: First find $\text{IQR}=Q_3-Q_1=32-20=12$.
Compute $1.5\cdot\text{IQR}=1.5\cdot 12=18$.
The upper fence is $Q_3+1.5\cdot\text{IQR}=32+18=50$.
Any value strictly greater than $50$ is a high outlier, so the upper fence is $50$.

items.prompt: Four students have quiz scores $14$, $16$, $18$, and $x$. The teacher wants the mean of the four scores to be exactly $20$. What value of $x$ is needed?

steps: The mean of the four scores is $\frac{14+16+18+x}{4}$, and we set it equal to $20$.
Multiply both sides by $4$: $48+x=80$.
Subtract $48$ from both sides: $x=80-48=32$.

items.prompt: Two data sets have the same mean of $50$. Set A is $\{48, 49, 50, 51, 52\}$ and Set B is $\{30, 40, 50, 60, 70\}$. Without computing the exact standard deviation, explain which set has the larger standard deviation and why.
items.answer: Set B has the larger standard deviation because its values lie much farther from the mean of $50$ than Set A's do.

steps: Standard deviation measures the typical distance of the values from the mean.
Both sets have the same mean, $50$, so we compare how far the values sit from $50$.
In Set A the values are at most $2$ away from $50$ (from $48$ to $52$), so deviations are tiny.
In Set B the values range from $30$ to $70$, up to $20$ away from $50$, so deviations are large.
Larger deviations from the mean produce a larger standard deviation, so Set B has the greater standard deviation.
